bull.b: Rapid QCaaS growth and a larger share of revenue from production applications indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation toward operational use. This supports a more repeatable software-and-services revenue base and strengthens D-Wave’s commercial credibility over the next several quarters.

Peer-reviewed validation of D-Wave’s dual-rail gate-model architecture provides external support for its technology roadmap, while its established annealing platform serves current use cases. Combining both approaches could broaden the addressable market and create a differentiated position as quantum adoption develops.

The sharp increase in remaining performance obligations and multiple production deployments provide evidence of customer conversion and future revenue visibility. Measurable operational outcomes across telecom and healthcare also support referenceability, which can help D-Wave expand enterprise adoption over the medium term.

bear.b: D-Wave remains far from profitability despite solid gross margins, because its cost structure produces very large operating and net losses. Continued negative cash generation reduces self-funding capacity and makes successful commercialization, cost control and eventual operating leverage essential to financial durability.

The sharp revenue decline shows that large system transactions can materially distort reported performance between periods. Management expects most 2026 revenue in Q4 from planned shipments, so delivery and installation timing remains a meaningful execution risk and limits near-term revenue predictability.

Although the funding can accelerate research, the structure introduces dilution and ongoing government oversight, including IP and transaction constraints. These conditions may reduce strategic flexibility and increase execution complexity while D-Wave works to meet milestones tied to the multi-year award.
